 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE AJAY DIGPAUL  ORDER % 19.12.2025 1.

The present petition has been filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 (hereinafter BNSS), read with Section 528 of the BNSS, on behalf of the petitioner seeking his enlargement on regular bail in connection with his custody arising out of FIR no. 91/2019 registered at Police Station Kalindi Kunj under Section 365/302/201/120B/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.

The facts arising out of the subject FIR are that on 16.03.2019, a secret informer informed HC Sharwan that a boy named Sajan from Aali Village who is constantly engaged in the commission of petty crimes from Badarpur to Kalkaji and Govindpuri is missing since the previous night, and that he was last seen consuming liquor in the jungle of Aali Village with Neeraj @ Prashant on the previous night, i.e., 15.03.2019.

The secret informer is further reported to have informed the police that Neeraj @ Prashant was hiding in the jungle of Aali Village and it appears as if he was trying to escape.
Upon the police reaching the said jungle, their secret informer aided in locating Neeraj @ Prashant who was apprehended while hiding in a bush.
4. Upon interrogation, it came to be known from Neeraj @ Prashant that Sajan was using obscene language and making lewd gestures at Neeraj's sister and was following her.

5. Neeraj further disclosed that in an attempt to teach Sajan a lesson, he invited him to the jungle on the pretext of drinking alcohol together.
When Sajan got drunk, Neeraj stated that he took him on a scooter towards Yamuna and stopped near a crematorium next to Shiv Ghat.
He then attacked Sajan with a knife and dragged him to the Yamuna to drown him.
6. Once satisfied that Sajan was dead, he went back to his house to change his clothes, throwing his blood stained clothes over the Lohia bridge into the Agra canal, along with the murder weapon.
On the police reaching Yamuna bank along with Neeraj, a dead body was recovered from the water.
7. The chargesheet reveals Neeraj's supplementary disclosure statement based upon which the petitioner, the youngest out of three of Neeraj's uncles, was implicated.

His supplementary disclosure further states that he had received information that the deceased made an obscene video of his cousin sister, due to which Neeraj and his uncles plotted the deceased's murder.
On 15.03.2019, Neeraj and the petitioner allegedly brought two knives from their house, and upon cornering the deceased near the This is a digitally signed order.

It is stated that the deceased was still alive at this point, and that Neeraj and the petitioner were beating the deceased in the car.
8. It was further disclosed that Neeraj and the petitioner once again attacked the deceased with a knife multiple times, and Neeraj strangled the deceased, after which he died.
After this, the deceased's body was state to have been dumped after Neeraj and his uncles had slit the deceased's throat numerous times.
9. After this, the accused persons dumped the body, got rid of the murder weapon, and cleaned the car of any evidence of the crime.

Lastly, it was also disclosed by Neeraj that the other co accused persons instructed him that incase is caught by the police, he must confess to the crime himself and state that he took the deceased on his scooter to Yamuna Ghat and stabbed him.
10. Based on this supplementary disclosure statement, the petitioner is stated to have been arrested on 18.03.2019 and taken into custody the next day.
11. The status report on record reiterated the same facts contained within the chargesheet as mentioned above, adding that the clothes of the petitioner were also recovered.
The FSL result is stated to have not been conclusively incriminating.
12. The report further states that 20 out of 51 prosecution witnesses have been examined, wherein all 10 public witnesses form a part.

13. The report stated that the petitioner is incriminated by virtue of statements of eyewitnesses,
CCTV footage, MLC/postmortem of the deceased, recoveries of blood stained clothes, recovery of the car allegedly utilized to commit the offence, CAF and CDR details, and disclosure statement of co-accused Neeraj.
14. The petitioner approached the learned ASJ seeking to be enlarged on regular bail, but the same was denied on two occasions vide orders dated 13.02.2024 and 07.11.2025.
The petitioner approached this Court seeking to be enlarged on bail, but his application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dared 09.10.2025.

15. Learned Counsel for the petitioner, Mr. Anil Vyas, submits that the petitioner has suffered a lengthy incarceration of nearly 7 years while less than half of the total number of prosecution witnesses have been examined, and that the petitioner has only been incriminated on the disclosure statement of co-accused Neeraj.
16. Mr. Vyas further submits that the petitioner has been acquitted in all four antecedents, and that these acquittals concluded more than a decade ago.
17. Ms. Meenakshi Dahiya, learned APP for the State, objects to the grant of bail to the petitioner on the ground of the seriousness of offences alleged, as well as his criminal antecedents.

18. Heard and perused.

21.

given that he has been acquitted in all of them and that the latest of these acquittals took place during the year 2013.
